chief_complaint: firm, painless lump on the right palm causing right ring finger to bend inward
hpi_details: 48F reports a firm, painless nodule on her right palm that has been present for 1 year. Over the past 3 months, a tight band has developed, pulling her right ring finger slightly inward toward the palm.
ideas: thinks she has a cyst or tendon strain

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Dupuytren Contracture is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Dupuytren Contracture of the palm, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Dupuytren Contracture.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Trigger finger (stenosing tenosynovitis) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Inability to place hand flat on table (Tabletop test positive).
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Dupuytren Contracture of the palm
Discuss treatment options based on contracture severity (observation, collagenase injection, or needle/open aponeurectomy)
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Fibroproliferative disease of the palmar fascia causing fixed flexion contracture of the MCP and PIP joints.
red_flags: Inability to place hand flat on table (Tabletop test positive)

must_ask.say: Are your ring or small fingers pulled inward toward your palm so you cannot straighten them?
Do you feel firm, painless bumps or tight cords under the skin of your palm?
Can you lay your hand completely flat face down on a table?
Does anyone in your family have similar bent fingers or feet cords?
Do you have diabetes, heavy alcohol intake, or liver disease?
